ID/status inventory is not a rule-description correctness score.

No latest-law or live-catalogue verification; source editions and local catalogue snapshot only.

Interpretation rules paraphrase OECD 2009 (non-binding) and EU wording as curated by rd-bridge; the OECD text itself was not available for verification.

findings.source: chemmon_docs/EFSA Supporting Publications - 2026 -  - Reporting guidance for use levels on food additives and food flavourings ‐ 2026.pdf
findings.observation: Description says typical or maximum cannot be zero; error message says neither is greater than zero and prints C10A instead of C19A.
findings.action: Record the source-supported interpretation and rationale; retain the exact source wording and implementation limits.
findings.resolution: Resolved as the strongest contextual interpretation: when presence includes C19A, typicalLevel>0 OR maxLevel>0, because the source error describes neither value being positive. With USE25 ordering satisfied, typical=0/max>0 satisfies this interpretation. C10A is a source typo; C19A is consistent in description and field examples. Moderately high confidence, independently corroborated; not live-validator verification.
